'''David Godfrey Pettifor''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|CBE|FRS}}<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sutton|first1=Adrian P.|last2=Drautz|first2=Ralf|last3=Vitek|first3=Vaclav|date=2019|title=David Godfrey Pettifor. 9 March 1945—16 October 2017|url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2018.0038|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=66|pages=329–353|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2018.0038|doi-access=free|hdl=10044/1/66793|s2cid=86518869|hdl-access=free}}</ref> (9 March 1945 – 16 October 2017<ref>[https://www.thetimes.com/uk/science/article/professor-david-pettifor-jv8dxf5bd Professor David Pettifor]</ref>) was the [[Isaac Wolfson]] Professor of [[Metallurgy]] at the [[University of Oxford]] from 1992 to 2011.<ref name="personal">{{cite web|url=http://www.materials.ox.ac.uk/peoplepages/pettifor.html|title=Personal Homepages|publisher=Oxford Materials|access-date=2 May 2011|archive-date=16 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171016201643/http://www.materials.ox.ac.uk/peoplepages/pettifor.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was also a [[Fellow]] of [[St Edmund Hall, Oxford]].<ref name="edmund">{{cite web|url=https://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/index.php?section=197|title=David Pettifor|publisher=St Edmund Hall|access-date=2 May 2011}}</ref>

He was the author of a book entitled ''Bonding and Structure of Molecules and Solids'' ([[Oxford University Press]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/story.asp?storyCode=163627&sectioncode=33|title=Simply bound to be desirable|date=9 February 1996|publisher=Times Higher Education|access-date=2 May 2011}}</ref>  He created "structure maps" which determine which crystal structure an alloy will form. He was a world authority on materials modelling and helped established the Oxford Materials Modelling Laboratory.

He held a [[BSc]] from the [[University of Witwatersrand]] in [[South Africa]] and a [[PhD]] from the [[University of Cambridge]], supervised by [[Volker Heine]].<ref name="edmund" />

He was made a [[Order of the British Empire|CBE]] in  the Queen's Birthday Honours in 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ox.ac.uk/media/news_stories/2005/050613.html |title=Queen's Birthday Honours 2005 |publisher=University of Oxford |access-date=2 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120930082500/http://www.ox.ac.uk/media/news_stories/2005/050613.html |archive-date=30 September 2012 }}</ref> In 1999, he received the Royal Society Armourers and Brasiers' Medal.<ref name="personal" /> Other awards include the William Hume-Rothery Award and the Hume-Rothery Prize.<ref name="personal" />

He died on 16 October 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/news/death-david-pettifor |title=Death of David Pettifor &#124; St Edmund Hall |access-date=2017-10-27 |archive-date=2017-10-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171027231516/https://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/news/death-david-pettifor |url-status=dead }}</ref>
